history: The second generation Dodge Neon arrived for the 2000 model year as a thorough revision of the original PL platform. While it retained the same basic architecture as the first generation, Chrysler's engineers addressed nearly every criticism leveled at its predecessor — refining the interior quality, improving NVH characteristics, and giving the car a more mature, grown-up personality without sacrificing the fun-to-drive character that made the original Neon a hit.

The most significant improvements came inside the cabin. The second-gen Neon featured a completely redesigned interior with higher quality materials, a more ergonomic dashboard layout, and significantly better sound insulation. Road and wind noise — persistent complaints about the first generation — were dramatically reduced, making the car far more livable as a daily driver.

Under the hood the 2.0-liter DOHC engine received minor refinements bringing torque output up slightly to 135 lb-ft. The Sport trim continued to offer this higher-output engine while the base model retained the SOHC unit. The 5-speed manual transmission was also revised with improved shift quality, addressing another first-gen criticism.

The second generation Neon served as the direct foundation for what would become the SRT-4. Chrysler's SRT division selected the revised PL platform for its performance project, recognizing that the second-gen Neon's stiffer structure and refined dynamics made it a better candidate for forced induction than its predecessor. Production of the standard second-gen Neon wrapped in 2002, with the SRT-4 carrying the Neon nameplate through 2005.
did_you_know: The second-generation Neon's body structure was significantly stiffer than the first generation — a key reason the SRT division chose it as the basis for the SRT-4. The improved torsional rigidity allowed the turbocharged drivetrain to put power down more effectively and gave the SRT-4 its surprisingly capable handling despite its budget origins.

trims.name: Neon Base
trims.description: The entry-level second-gen Neon with the SOHC engine, improved interior quality over the first generation, and standard dual airbags and ABS.

trims.name: Neon ES
trims.description: A new mid-tier trim replacing the Highline, adding cruise control, upgraded cloth seating, and additional convenience features at a modest price premium.

trims.name: Neon Sport
trims.description: The DOHC-equipped performance trim with sport suspension tuning, 15-inch alloy wheels, and the revised close-ratio 5-speed manual transmission.

trims.name: Neon R/T
trims.description: The top-of-the-line performance trim returning for 2001 with the DOHC engine, sport-tuned Koni shocks, unique badging, and the closest preview of what the SRT-4 would become.

variants.name: Neon R/T
variants.description: The R/T made a welcome return for 2001 after a brief absence. With Koni shocks, the DOHC engine, and a sport-tuned suspension, it was the ultimate expression of the second-gen Neon and a clear preview of the SRT-4's potential.

variants.name: Neon ACR
variants.description: The American Club Racer package continued into the second generation, offering Koni adjustable shocks, a strut tower brace, and stripped interior for maximum track performance on a budget.

variants.name: Chrysler PT Cruiser (Related)
variants.description: While not a Neon variant, the PT Cruiser used a modified version of the same PL platform. Its development alongside the second-gen Neon helped Chrysler amortize engineering costs across both models.
